medicaid_program_name: Medicaid / Medical Assistance (MA); managed care is called HealthChoices (Physical, Behavioral and Community HealthChoices). Adult expansion group: 'Adults ages 19-64' under MAGI rules.
medicaid_adult_income_limit_note: PA DHS Medicaid page table 'Medicaid Income Requirements 138% of Federal Poverty Income Guidelines', 'Effective: January 13, 2026': household of 1 $22,025/year, 2 $29,864, 3 $37,702, 4 $45,540, each additional $7,839. DHS General Eligibility page lists 'Adults ages 19-64 with incomes at or below 133 percent of the Federal Income Poverty Guidelines (FPIG)' (133% plus the standard 5% MAGI disregard = 138%; the two pages are consistent in effect). 2027 changes (DHS 'Changes Coming to Medicaid in Pennsylvania'): starting January 1, 2027, work and community engagement requirements apply to adult recipients ages 19-64 who do not have a dependent child under 14 and do not meet an exemption (80 hours/month of work, training, school, etc., or household monthly income of at least $580); current recipients report at their next 2027 renewal; some expansion adults move to six-month renewals; retroactive coverage for expansion adults drops to one month.

state_subsidy_or_reinsurance_note: Pennsylvania's Section 1332 Waiver Reinsurance Program (authorized by Act 42 of 2019) partially reimburses insurers for high-cost individual-market claims, funded by Pennie plus federal pass-through savings. First approved in 2020 (plan years 2021-2025); an extension approved in 2025 continues it January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2030, so it is in effect for 2027. It is 'invisible' to consumers (no application). No separate state-funded premium subsidy for 2027 was found on pennie.com or the PID site.
state_subsidy_quote: An application to extend the waiver was approved in 2025, continuing the program from January 1, 2026, through December 31, 2030.

state_subsidy_extra_quotes.quote: partially reimburse insurance companies for costs associated with high-cost claims in the individual market.
The reimbursement allows insurers to set lower premiums for all individuals purchasing their health insurance through the individual market.
Pennsylvania's reinsurance program is "invisible" to consumers, who continue to enroll in coverage and seek care under their policies
approved Pennsylvania's extension request under section 1332 of the ACA. This approval is effective for January 1, 2026, through December 31, 2030.
For 2027, the Pennsylvania Insurance Department has mandated that an adjustment factor of 1.0 is applied ... state-based reinsurance program
state_subsidy_extra_quotes.note: Insurer-written 2027 rate filing posted on the PID site; supports that the program is built into 2027 rates. Not for copy (names an insurer).

copy.medicaid: Pennsylvania has expanded Medicaid for adults age 19 to 64. The state’s Medicaid income table, effective January 13, 2026, lists yearly income up to $22,025 for one person and $45,540 for a household of four. Starting January 1, 2027, some adults age 19 to 64 without a child under 14 must meet work requirements or qualify for an exemption.
copy.state_help: Pennsylvania has a state reinsurance program. It pays insurers back for part of the cost of high-cost claims on health plans people buy for themselves. People do not apply for it. It is approved through December 31, 2030.

notes_unverified: OE end date: Pennie's FAQ (modified Nov 6, 2026), how-to-enroll page and 2027 'What's New' page (published Sept 18, modified Nov 1, 2026) say Nov 1 - Jan 15; none of them prints the year '2027' next to January 15. The 2027 OE press releases (Oct 22, Nov 6 and Nov 10, 2026) give the Nov 1 start and the Dec 15 deadline but not the end date. For 2026 coverage Pennie extended both its first deadline (release Dec 16, 2025) and its final deadline to Jan 31, 2026 (releases Jan 7 and Jan 22, 2026). No 2027 extension announced as of Nov 24, 2026. Re-check pennie.com before publishing.

Medicaid limit wording: DHS's General Eligibility page says 'at or below 133 percent' while the DHS Medicaid page table is titled '138% of Federal Poverty Income Guidelines'. They agree once the federal 5-percentage-point MAGI disregard (42 CFR 435.603(d)(4)) is counted; copy uses the 138% table's dollar figures. The DHS table itself is not labeled 'adults'; it is a general MAGI Medicaid table, which matches the adult group limit.

State help: only the 1332 reinsurance program was found. No separate state-funded premium subsidy for 2027 was found on pennie.com (including the Affordability page), the Pennie press releases, or the PID site. This is an absence finding, not an official statement.

Not used in copy: the PID page's claim that premiums fell '4-6% annually' under reinsurance (a statistic), and its statement that reinsurance lets insurers 'set lower premiums' (a price claim, removed from copy by the checker).

Other 2027 items not used in copy: from 2027 only lawful permanent residents, Cuban/Haitian entrants and COFA residents among non-citizens remain eligible for Pennie financial savings (Pennie What's New); some adults 19-64 move to six-month Medicaid renewals; retroactive coverage for expansion adults drops to one month (DHS).
No KFF or other secondary source was used for Pennsylvania.
